userStories.title: Describe note-only memory inputs in thread and MCP catalogs
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Change the shared koda_add_memory descriptor and its MCP wording to offer notes only.

**Motivation** — Thread memories never reach nax runs.

**Approach** — Target: `inputSchema` is `{ type: 'object', additionalProperties: false, required: ['slug', 'type', 'description', 'body'], properties: { slug, type, description, body } }`. `slug` carries `pattern` = `MEMORY_NOTE_SLUG_RE.source`; `type` carries `enum` = `MEMORY_NOTE_TYPES`; `description` has `minLength: 1`, `maxLength: MEMORY_NOTE_DESCRIPTION_MAX_CHARS`; `body` has `minLength: 1`, `maxLength: MEMORY_NOTE_BODY_MAX_BYTES`. The tool description says it remembers one note in the project's memory, names the four types with one line each on when to use them (`project`: how this project works; `feedback`: a rule or agreement on how to work; `reference`: where something is or how a tool behaves; `user`: about a person), and keeps the existing approval and `koda_record_decision` sentences. The `MEMORY_WRITE_KINDS` constant in this file is removed.

For `MCP_DESCRIPTIONS.koda_add_memory` in `apps/api/src/fleet/assistant/mcp/mcp-tool-catalog.ts`: Target: the first sentence says the call remembers one note in this project's memory and names the four note types; the remaining sentences ("The call runs at once as the calling agent, ..." and the project sentence) are kept as they are. Keep the existing decision-routing sentence too. MCP agents read this text, not the descriptor's.

**Scope** — In: modify koda-tool-descriptors.ts, mcp/mcp-tool-catalog.ts and their existing specs. Out: parser/preview/execute changes belong to US-002; real entry-point proof belongs to US-003; repository search belongs to US-004/US-005. `koda_record_decision`, `koda_memory_search` and `koda_get_memory` keep their input schemas. Do not change WORKSPACE project injection. `koda_add_memory` keeps writing project-scope notes only; a `scope` field for user notes is not added. nax is not changed: its koda provider keeps mirroring and searching NOTE rows only. 
**Interface** — Reuse the existing note constants, unchanged:
```ts
MEMORY_NOTE_SLUG_RE = /^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,63}$/
MEMORY_NOTE_TYPES = ['user', 'feedback', 'project', 'reference']
MEMORY_NOTE_BODY_MAX_BYTES = 8192
MEMORY_NOTE_DESCRIPTION_MAX_CHARS = 200
```
The schema has exactly slug, type, description and body as string properties, all required; no kind. Constants above are illustrative assignments from the spec, not new definitions to duplicate.

**Existing assertions to modify** — `apps/api/src/fleet/assistant/koda-tool-descriptors.spec.ts` — it asserts `KODA_ADD_MEMORY.inputSchema.required` is kind, subject, predicate (line ~260), the kind enum of five kinds (lines ~293-306), the subject and predicate 1..200 bounds and the object maxLength 8192 (lines ~333-337), and that kind excludes DECISION (line ~345); these become assertions on the slug, type, description and body properties as the US-001 ACs state, never deleted outright.
`apps/api/src/fleet/assistant/mcp/mcp-tool-catalog.spec.ts` — one new case for the `koda_add_memory` MCP description is added; no existing assertion changes, and the description keeps the sentences its existing cases check (runs at once as the calling agent, the action id, the MCP sentence).

**Verification** — Use failing descriptor/catalog unit cases first, then implement. The descriptor file's MEMORY_WRITE_KINDS removal is verified by `bunx turbo type-check` and `bunx turbo lint` reporting no remaining reference, not by an AC. Do not remove shared constants still used by other descriptors.
acceptanceCriteria: AC-1 [unit] KODA_ADD_MEMORY.inputSchema.required equals ['slug', 'type', 'description', 'body'].
AC-2 [unit] KODA_ADD_MEMORY.inputSchema.properties.type.enum equals MEMORY_NOTE_TYPES (user, feedback, project, reference).
AC-3 [unit] KODA_ADD_MEMORY.inputSchema.properties.slug.pattern equals MEMORY_NOTE_SLUG_RE.source.
AC-4 [unit] KODA_ADD_MEMORY.inputSchema.properties.description has minLength 1 and maxLength 200.
AC-5 [unit] KODA_ADD_MEMORY.inputSchema.properties.body.maxLength equals MEMORY_NOTE_BODY_MAX_BYTES (8192).
AC-6 [unit] KODA_ADD_MEMORY.inputSchema.properties has no kind property.
AC-7 [unit] KODA_ADD_MEMORY.inputSchema.additionalProperties is false.
AC-8 [unit] KODA_ADD_MEMORY.description names each of `user`, `feedback`, `project` and `reference` in backticks.
AC-9 [unit] The koda_add_memory description returned by mcpToolDescriptors() names each of `user`, `feedback`, `project` and `reference` in backticks.

routing.reasoning: Two existing catalog implementations and two unit specs; standard schema/wording changes with no authorization logic or new abstractions.

modifiedFiles.reason: it asserts `KODA_ADD_MEMORY.inputSchema.required` is kind, subject, predicate (line ~260), the kind enum of five kinds (lines ~293-306), the subject and predicate 1..200 bounds and the object maxLength 8192 (lines ~333-337), and that kind excludes DECISION (line ~345); these become assertions on the slug, type, description and body properties as the US-001 ACs state, never deleted outright.

one new case for the `koda_add_memory` MCP description is added; no existing assertion changes, and the description keeps the sentences its existing cases check (runs at once as the calling agent, the action id, the MCP sentence).

userStories.title: Parse, preview and persist note-only memory writes
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Map koda_add_memory's four note fields to the existing NOTE validation, preview and upsert path.

**Motivation** — In the live check, a thread agent asked to save two durable facts chose CONSTRAINT and PREFERENCE, because `koda_add_memory` offers those kinds first.

**Approach** — Target: `AddMemoryInput = { slug: string; type: string; description: string; body: string }`. `parse` reads exactly those four keys (any other key, including a legacy `kind`, `subject`, `predicate`, `object` or `ownerId`, is dropped), builds the candidate `{ kind: MemoryKind.NOTE, subject: slug, predicate: type, object: body, description }` and judges it with `noteFieldError`. The field it names is translated to the tool's own name: `subject` -> `slug`, `predicate` -> `type`, `object` -> `body`, `description` -> `description`. Field checks run in this order: first a type check of each field in the order `slug`, `type`, `body`, `description` (a missing or non-string field refuses with that field's own name), then `noteFieldError` on the candidate. The JSON schema limits are advisory for the model: `body.maxLength` counts characters, while `parse` enforces the 8192-byte cap through `noteFieldError`. `preview` and `execute` keep their current behaviour with `kind` fixed to `NOTE`, `subject` = slug, `predicate` = type, `object` = body. The preview header stays `Remember in <projectSlug>: NOTE <slug> / <type>`, followed by the description line, the body, and the `Replaces memory:<id>` line when an active note has that slug. `MemoryWriteKind`, `MEMORY_WRITE_KINDS`, `MAX_KEY_CHARS` and `MAX_OBJECT_CHARS` are removed from this file. Both `MEMORY_WRITE_KINDS` definitions go (one in `koda-tool-descriptors.ts`, one in `add-memory-tool.ts`); the removals are verified by `bunx turbo type-check` and `bunx turbo lint` reporting no remaining reference, not by an AC. US-001 owns the descriptor-file removal.

Symbols read unchanged: `noteFieldError(input: MemoryNoteInput): MemoryNoteField | null` in `apps/api/src/memory/memory-note.ts`, where `MemoryNoteField = 'subject' | 'predicate' | 'object' | 'description'`. It is the one note validator; `POST /memory` calls it too. `buildActiveKey(...)` in `apps/api/src/memory/prisma-memory-item.repository.ts`: a NOTE's active key is `NOTE:<subject>`, so re-saving a slug with a new type supersedes the old note. `ToolInputError(reason)` in `apps/api/src/fleet/assistant/assistant-tool.types.ts`; the agent reads `invalid_input: <reason>`.

**Scope** — In: change add-memory-tool.ts and update its unit suite plus origin-tools.spec.ts and assistant.module.spec.ts fixtures. Out: descriptor/MCP wording is US-001; runner/MCP/database end-to-end proofs are US-003; search is US-004/US-005. `koda_add_memory` keeps writing project-scope notes only; a `scope` field for user notes is not added. `POST /memory`, `POST /memory/decisions`, `POST /memory/extract`, the CLI `memory create` command and ticket-event memory keep accepting and writing every kind they write today; only the `koda_add_memory` tool narrows to notes. Approval requests for `koda_add_memory` that are still pending at deploy time and carry a legacy triple input are not migrated; approving one after deploy answers `invalid_input: slug`. US-002 only: the note limits (slug pattern, 200-character description, 8192-byte body) are not re-pinned through the tool; `noteFieldError`'s existing specs pin them, and the tool only translates the field name it reports. US-002 only: the preview's `Replaces memory:<id>` line keeps its current behaviour; the existing cases that pin it are rewritten to note inputs under `### Modifies`, not re-specified.

**Interface**
```ts
AddMemoryInput = { slug: string; type: string; description: string; body: string }
noteFieldError(input: MemoryNoteInput): MemoryNoteField | null
MemoryNoteField = 'subject' | 'predicate' | 'object' | 'description'
```
Retain the existing factory's dependency interface and AssistantTool<AddMemoryInput> return type. Keep accepted strings as written, not trimmed. All type checks finish before the shared validator is called.

**Failure handling** — Missing/non-string slug refuses invalid_input: slug; invalid type refuses invalid_input: type. The existing validator's slug/type/body/description failures are translated to the tool field names, including blank descriptions, blank bodies and existing size-limit failures, without duplicating the limits. A legacy triple without slug refuses invalid_input: slug and creates no proposal. Re-saving a slug another principal's active note holds is refused forbidden naming memory.update, as today. Retain preview assertMayReplace, execute's in-transaction replaceCheck and audit hook, confidence 0.8, actor owner id/type, project selection, sourceType/sourceId attribution, preview masking and saved result text. Do not migrate pending triple approvals.

**Existing assertions to modify** — `apps/api/src/fleet/assistant/tools/add-memory-tool.spec.ts` — its parse, preview and execute cases build triple inputs (kind FACT with subject, predicate, object) and assert the five-kind list, the 4000-character triple object limit and that a triple carrying a description is refused; the tool now takes slug, type, description and body only, so these cases are rewritten to note inputs (the Replaces-line preview cases keep their assertions with a NOTE active item), and the triple-only cases are replaced by the note-field refusals in the US-002 ACs.
`apps/api/src/fleet/assistant/tools/origin-tools.spec.ts` — it parses the triple kind FACT, subject s, predicate p, which now refuses for slug; the input becomes a valid note (slug, type, description, body) and the origin assertion is unchanged.
`apps/api/src/fleet/assistant/assistant.module.spec.ts` — its per-key input map gives memory.create the triple kind FACT with subject, predicate and object; that entry becomes a valid note input so the write-tool registration cases keep parsing.

**Verification** — Strict three-session TDD protects owner-based replace checks and caller-supplied key dropping. Use the existing toolDeps/upsert spies. The three-line preview assertion uses AC-1's single-line body fixture; Markdown bodies may contain newlines and must not be collapsed to satisfy that assertion. Failure-table criteria below assert required-field errors and shared-validator name translation, not duplicate numeric-boundary tests. Exercise returned validator-field mappings without re-pinning numeric limits; memory-note.spec.ts remains their owner. Preserve existing permission, provenance, masking, audit and replacement regressions while rewriting their inputs.
acceptanceCriteria: AC-1 [unit] addMemoryTool(...).parse({ slug: 'deploy-steps', type: 'project', description: 'How to deploy', body: 'Run deploy.sh' }) returns exactly { slug: 'deploy-steps', type: 'project', description: 'How to deploy', body: 'Run deploy.sh' }.
AC-2 [unit] parse given that valid note plus ownerId: 'someone-else' and kind: 'FACT' returns exactly the same four note fields.

AC-3 [unit] Given { slug: 'deploy-steps', type: 'project', description: 'How to deploy', body: 'Run deploy.sh' } with only slug changed to 'Deploy Steps', parse throws ToolInputError whose reason is slug.

AC-4 [unit] Given { slug: 'deploy-steps', type: 'project', description: 'How to deploy', body: 'Run deploy.sh' } with only type changed to 'constraint', parse throws ToolInputError whose reason is type.
AC-5 [unit] Given { slug: 'deploy-steps', type: 'project', description: 'How to deploy', body: 'Run deploy.sh' } with description omitted, parse throws ToolInputError whose reason is description.
AC-6 [unit] Given { slug: 'deploy-steps', type: 'project', description: 'How to deploy', body: 'Run deploy.sh' } with only body changed to '   ', parse throws ToolInputError whose reason is body.
AC-7 [unit] parse({ kind: 'FACT', subject: 'api', predicate: 'runs on', object: 'bun' }) throws ToolInputError whose reason is slug.
AC-8 [unit] parse({ slug: 'Bad Slug', type: 5, description: 'd', body: 'b' }) throws ToolInputError whose reason is type, because type checks run before noteFieldError.

AC-9 [unit] Given { slug: 'deploy-steps', type: 'project', description: 'How to deploy', body: 'Run deploy.sh' } and no active note of that slug, preview answers exactly Remember in <projectSlug>: NOTE deploy-steps / project, then How to deploy, then Run deploy.sh, as three newline-separated lines.
AC-10 [unit] execute of a valid note calls the repository upsert with kind NOTE, subject = slug, predicate = type, object = body and description as given.

Failure handling [unit] When required fields are missing or non-string, parse throws ToolInputError whose reason is the first such field in slug, type, body, description order, before judging string content.

Failure handling [unit] Given four string note fields, when noteFieldError reports subject, predicate, object or description for the NOTE candidate, parse throws ToolInputError whose reason is respectively slug, type, body or description (for example a blank description refuses with reason description).

routing.reasoning: One tool implementation and three existing unit suites, with a clear mapping and no new abstraction; strict security override applies to owner-id dropping and preservation of permission-gated supersession in preview/execute.

modifiedFiles.reason: its parse, preview and execute cases build triple inputs (kind FACT with subject, predicate, object) and assert the five-kind list, the 4000-character triple object limit and that a triple carrying a description is refused; the tool now takes slug, type, description and body only, so these cases are rewritten to note inputs (the Replaces-line preview cases keep their assertions with a NOTE active item), and the triple-only cases are replaced by the note-field refusals in the US-002 ACs.
it parses the triple kind FACT, subject s, predicate p, which now refuses for slug; the input becomes a valid note (slug, type, description, body) and the origin assertion is unchanged.
its per-key input map gives memory.create the triple kind FACT with subject, predicate and object; that entry becomes a valid note input so the write-tool registration cases keep parsing.

userStories.title: Integrate note-only writes through runner approval and MCP
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Prove the note-only tool through its real runner/approval and MCP entry points while adapting the affected integration fixtures.

**Motivation** — Both were stored in koda and are invisible to every nax run.

**Approach** — Prove the note-only tool through its real entry points: the runner tool-call route a thread uses (propose, approve, stored NOTE, supersede by slug) and the MCP call path (a legacy triple is refused). Rewrite the existing integration specs that propose FACT triples through `koda_add_memory` to note inputs.

`buildActiveKey(...)` in `apps/api/src/memory/prisma-memory-item.repository.ts`: a NOTE's active key is `NOTE:<subject>`, so re-saving a slug with a new type supersedes the old note. `ToolInputError(reason)` in `apps/api/src/fleet/assistant/assistant-tool.types.ts`; the agent reads `invalid_input: <reason>`. `preview` and `execute` keep their current behaviour with `kind` fixed to `NOTE`, `subject` = slug, `predicate` = type, `object` = body. The preview header stays `Remember in <projectSlug>: NOTE <slug> / <type>`, followed by the description line, the body, and the `Replaces memory:<id>` line when an active note has that slug.

**Scope** — In: update the three existing integration specs, adding thread approval/same-slug supersession and legacy MCP refusal proofs. Out: descriptor/parser implementation belongs to US-001/US-002; search recall belongs to US-004/US-005. US-003 consumes US-001's descriptor and US-002's tool through the existing runner tool-call route and MCP path; neither adds a new exported symbol. US-003 only: the `forbidden` refusal for replacing another principal's note keeps its current behaviour; the existing permissions case that pins it is rewritten to note inputs under `### Modifies`, not re-specified. Existing non-note rows and general POST /memory FACT writers are not converted.

**Interface**
```ts
AddMemoryInput = { slug: string; type: string; description: string; body: string }
```
Use the existing runner route `POST /api/fleet/runner/jobs/:jobId/tools/koda_add_memory?leaseEpoch=1` with toolCallId/input and the holding runner key for dev's RUNNING thread job. Decide through `POST /api/approvals/:id/decisions` as dev. Use the existing mcpCall/callTool helpers for `/api/mcp` tools/call, with the required project slug in MCP arguments. No exported production interface is added.

**Modifies** — `apps/api/test/integration/fleet/assistant-add-memory-tool.integration.spec.ts` — its ITEM constant (line ~41), the storedItems/storedItem lookups (lines ~69, ~75) and the beforeEach cleanup (line ~125) key on the FACT triple api / runs on, and its preview assertion expects a header naming FACT; ITEM becomes a note with one fixed slug whose body keeps the word bun (its AC-12 searches text bun), the lookups and the cleanup key on kind NOTE and that slug (the cleanup deletes every row of the slug so no Replaces line leaks between cases), and the preview assertion expects the NOTE header followed by the description and body lines.
`apps/api/test/integration/memory/permissions-memory-routes.integration.spec.ts` — AC-14 seeds the FACT key ac14:tool / uses through postMemory (which hardcodes kind FACT) and reads it back through the rows and activeRow helpers (which filter kind FACT and key on subject and predicate); the seed passes extra kind NOTE with subject ac14-tool, predicate project and a description, the rows and activeRow helpers filter kind NOTE and key on the slug alone, the MCP call sends slug ac14-tool with type feedback and a body, and the case first asserts the seeded item is defined, then keeps the assertions that the call is refused naming memory.update and the seeded item is still active and unchanged. Apply NOTE+slug lookups specifically to this case via a compatible helper option or note-specific helper; other callers of shared rows/activeRow still test FACT behavior and must not change to NOTE.
`apps/api/test/integration/audit/audit-memory-system.integration.spec.ts` — its `koda_add_memory` MCP calls send kind FACT triples and one assertion expects the audit summary created FACT (line ~219); the calls become valid note inputs keeping the slugs tool (line ~227) and tool-fail (line ~266), the failure case stays a valid note so it still reaches the audit failure path rather than an invalid_input refusal, and the summary assertion expects created NOTE.

**Verification** — This is an explicitly prescribed integration story, not a new production abstraction. Strict three-session TDD applies to authenticated runner/MCP calls, approval attribution and preserved permissions checks. Retain all existing audit rollback/provenance and bun readback assertions. Use canRunDbTests and run the three modified integration files with test:scoped against real test Postgres outside the sandbox; skipped database tests do not verify the story. Clean all versions of the fixed NOTE slug between cases so prior supersessions cannot affect previews. For the pending/no-memory assertion, count all statuses for that project and slug, not only active rows. For the refused legacy MCP case, query subject ac15:tool without a kind restriction so a wrongly created FACT cannot escape the no-row assertion.
acceptanceCriteria: AC-1 [integration] Through the runner tool-call route that assistant-add-memory-tool.integration.spec.ts drives, the runner holding dev's RUNNING thread job calls koda_add_memory with a valid note and is answered pending.
AC-2 [integration] While that proposal waits for dev, the project has no memory item with that slug.
AC-3 [integration] After dev approves it through POST /api/approvals/:id/decisions, the project has exactly one active memory item of kind NOTE with that slug as subject.
AC-4 [integration] That stored item carries the proposed type as predicate, the proposed body as object and the proposed description as description.
AC-5 [integration] A second proposal with the same slug and a different type, once approved, leaves exactly one active NOTE for the slug, and it carries the new type.
AC-6 [integration] After that second approval, the item stored by the first approval has status superseded.

AC-7 [integration] In permissions-memory-routes.integration.spec.ts, an agent's MCP koda_add_memory call with { project, kind: 'FACT', subject: 'ac15:tool', predicate: 'uses', object: 'x' } answers invalid_input: slug.
AC-8 [integration] After that refused MCP call, the project has no memory item whose subject is ac15:tool.

routing.reasoning: Three existing integration suites already provide runner, approval, MCP and audit harnesses; fixture conversion and added supersession/refusal cases need no new integration abstraction, while the ownership-permission regression requires the security override.

modifiedFiles.reason: its ITEM constant (line ~41), the storedItems/storedItem lookups (lines ~69, ~75) and the beforeEach cleanup (line ~125) key on the FACT triple api / runs on, and its preview assertion expects a header naming FACT; ITEM becomes a note with one fixed slug whose body keeps the word bun (its AC-12 searches text bun), the lookups and the cleanup key on kind NOTE and that slug (the cleanup deletes every row of the slug so no Replaces line leaks between cases), and the preview assertion expects the NOTE header followed by the description and body lines.

AC-14 seeds the FACT key ac14:tool / uses through postMemory (which hardcodes kind FACT) and reads it back through the rows and activeRow helpers (which filter kind FACT and key on subject and predicate); the seed passes extra kind NOTE with subject ac14-tool, predicate project and a description, this case reads the seed back with its own kind NOTE lookup keyed on the slug alone (the shared rows and activeRow helpers keep filtering kind FACT for the other cases in the file), the MCP call sends slug ac14-tool with type feedback and a body, and the case first asserts the seeded item is defined, then keeps the assertions that the call is refused naming memory.update and the seeded item is still active and unchanged.

its `koda_add_memory` MCP calls send kind FACT triples and one assertion expects the audit summary created FACT (line ~219); the calls become valid note inputs keeping the slugs tool (line ~227) and tool-fail (line ~266), the failure case stays a valid note so it still reaches the audit failure path rather than an invalid_input refusal, and the summary assertion expects created NOTE.

userStories.title: Add guarded any-word search before description-aware substring fallback
acceptanceCriteria: AC-1 [unit] The lexeme probe's SQL selects numnode(websearch_to_tsquery( and ::text AS "query", binding the search text and english.
AC-2 [unit] When the probe answers lexemes 1 with no query, and the all-words ranked query matches nothing, findByProjectMemory issues exactly three raw queries before the substring path.

AC-3 [unit] When the probe answers query 'deploy' & !'backup' and the all-words query matches nothing, no further raw query runs after the probe and all-words ids/count queries before the substring path (exactly three raw queries in total), preserving the existing negated-search fallback.
AC-4 [unit] When the probe answers query 'deploy' & 'backup' and the all-words query matches nothing, the fourth raw query's SQL contains replace( and ' | ')::tsquery.

AC-5 [unit] When the probe answers query 'deploy' & 'backup', the all-words pass has total 0, and the any-word ids query answers ids mem-2, mem-1 with count 2, findByProjectMemory returns records in the order mem-2, mem-1 and memoryItem.count is not called.

AC-6 [unit] When the probe answers query 'deploy' & 'backup' and both ranked passes match nothing, the substring path's text term is an OR over subject, predicate, object and description, each a case-insensitive contains of the text.
AC-7 [unit] When the probe answers query 'deploy' & 'backup' and the all-words query matches rows, exactly three raw queries run.

Failure handling [unit] When search text yields one lexeme with no ' & ' in the probe's query and the all-words pass matches nothing, findByProjectMemory proceeds to the substring fallback without an any-word pass.

routing.reasoning: One repository and its existing SQL-spy unit suite gain a probe value and a second query expression; the same ranked-query builder reuses unchanged read-scope and filter predicates, with no authentication or authorization-rule changes.

suggestedCriteria: When the probe's query is null and the all-words pass has total 0, findByProjectMemory reaches substring fallback after exactly three raw queries.
When an all-words pass has total greater than zero but an empty requested page, findByProjectMemory returns that empty ranked page and its total without trying a later pass.

modifiedFiles.reason: the substring cases (the textTerm helper and the falls-back-to-contains case) assert the text term is an OR over exactly subject, predicate and object; the term now also matches description, so those expected objects gain the description contains term with mode insensitive. The ranked() helper gains an optional probe query value (default none, so existing cases keep a probe row without query). The probe assertion (probe SQL contains numnode(websearch_to_tsquery( ) stays true by the Target's no-alias probe form.

userStories.title: Prove search recall and ranking through PostgreSQL and API consumers
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Verify any-word ranking/filtering/paging and description substring recall through the existing database, REST and thread search harnesses.

**Motivation** — No query returned a wrong note, so recall, not precision, is the gap.

**Approach** — Prove the any-word pass and the description fallback against a real database: ranking by matched words, the default TTL filter, the kind filter, paging, an explicit order, the REST route (`GET /projects/:slug/memory?text=`) and the `koda_memory_search` tool.

The any-word pass is plain Postgres full-text search over the existing generated `searchVector` column and its index. No migration, no embeddings, no synonym dictionary. `ts_rank` over an OR query scores a row higher when it holds more of the query's lexemes, so the note that matches most words of a question comes first.

Integration symbols read unchanged: `MemoryGovernanceService.getProjectMemory` and the `koda_memory_search` tool (`apps/api/src/fleet/assistant/tools/knowledge-tools.ts`): both reach `PrismaMemoryItemRepository.findByProjectMemory` with the caller's `text`. The REST route `GET /projects/:slug/memory?text=` reaches the same method. `ContextBuilderService` calls it with no `text` and is unaffected.

**Scope** — In: add cases to memory-full-text-search.integration.spec.ts and assistant-memory-tools.integration.spec.ts using their existing DB/REST/executor harnesses. Out: repository implementation is US-004; note descriptor/parser/approval behavior belongs to US-001/US-002/US-003. US-005 consumes US-004's repository change through `GET /projects/:slug/memory` and `koda_memory_search`; US-004 adds no new exported symbol. US-005 only: the any-word pass reuses the all-words query's filter list unchanged, so the status, soft-delete, project-scope and subject-prefix filters are pinned by one representative case each in the existing full-text specs, not repeated per pass. `koda_memory_search` keeps its input schema; do not add search-pass metadata or change the generated vector/index.

**Interface** — Consume the existing method and entry points, unchanged:
```ts
async findByProjectMemory(query: ProjectMemoryQuery, page: IPageOption): Promise<IPageResult<MemoryItem>>
```
`GET /projects/:slug/memory?text=` returns the existing paginated memory response through the guarded route. `koda_memory_search` receives `{ text }` in a thread and returns the existing memory:<id> listing; note bodies stay out of the index listing.

**Fixtures** — five notes in one project, each `kind` NOTE, active, `predicate` `project`, subjects `note-a` to `note-e`, descriptions `label a` to `label e`, with these bodies: A `API integration specs need the compose test Postgres on port 5433.`; B `Run web unit tests with bunx jest.`; C `When a budget window is exceeded, dispatch pauses.`; D `Deploy runs build-images then deploy.sh, which takes a backup.`; E `Restore from the newest dump.` E's `updatedAt` is set later than D's.
Use these fixtures in the repository quality cases; seed the relevant additional expired NOTE/FACT for filter cases and the Chinese description/body for the REST case. Keep times explicit so newer E cannot accidentally validate rank-based D-before-E.

**Modifies** — `apps/api/test/integration/memory/memory-full-text-search.integration.spec.ts` — new any-word and description cases are added beside the existing ones; no existing assertion changes.
`apps/api/test/integration/fleet/assistant-memory-tools.integration.spec.ts` — one new `koda_memory_search` case is added that creates its own note C (updatedAt older than every shared seed row) and deletes it afterwards, so the shared seed's page and total assertions are unchanged.
Use a local create/delete in try/finally, not an extra permanent shared seed. A direct Prisma create may supply description even if the suite's existing Item helper does not yet accept it.

**Verification** — This remains its own integration-focused story under the binding structure. Write the new observable repository/REST/tool cases first, then consume US-004; do not weaken existing assertions to accommodate fixture pollution.
